{{short description|Polish mathematician (1932–2012}}
{{refimprove|date=December 2021}}
[[File:Aleksander Pełczyński grób.JPG|thumb|Pełczyński's grave in Warsaw]]

'''Aleksander "Olek" Pełczyński''' (2 July 1932, [[Ternopil|Tarnopol]], [[Second Polish Republic|Poland]] – 20 December 2012, [[Wrocław]]) was a Polish mathematician who worked in [[functional analysis]].<ref>Joe Diestel (ed.), [http://www.ams.org/publications/journals/notices/201701/rnoti-p54.pdf Aleksander "Olek" Pełczyński 1932–2012], [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 64, 2017, no.1, pp. 54–58</ref><ref>biographical införmation from ''Studia Mathematica'' 159 (1) (2003)</ref>

==Career==
Pełczyński studied mathematics from 1950 to 1956 at the [[University of Warsaw]] and received there his doctorate in 1958 under [[Stanisław Mazur]] with dissertation ''Własności izomorficzne przestrzeni Banacha związane ze słabą zbieżnością bezwarunkową szeregów'' (Isomorphic properties of [[Banach space]]s with regard to unconditional convergence of series).<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=45917|name=Aleksander Pełczyński}}</ref> From 1967 to 2002 he worked at the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].

From 1967 onwards, he was a member of the editorial staff of the journal ''[[Studia Mathematica]]''.

His doctoral students include [[Nicole Tomczak-Jaegermann]] and [[Stanisław Szarek]].

He died in December 2012<ref>[http://www.ptm.org.pl/zawartosc/zmar%C5%82-profesor-aleksander-pe%C5%82czy%C5%84ski-1932-2012 Zmarł Profesor Aleksander Pełczyński (1932-2012)] (Polish)</ref> and was buried in Warsaw.

==Research==
Pełczyński's main field of research was [[functional analysis]], especially the theory of [[Banach space]]s. The [[Bessaga–Pełczyński selection principle]] and the [[Pełczyński decomposition method]] are associated with his name.

==Awards and honors==
Pełczyński received the [[Stefan Banach Prize]] in 1961. In 1986, he was elected a member of the [[Akademie der Wissenschaften der DDR]]. He received the [[Stefan Banach Medal]] of the Polish Academy of Sciences in 1996. In 2005, he was granted an honorary doctorate from the [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań]].

In 1966, Pełczyński was (with [[Boris Mityagin]]) an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Moscow.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Aizerman, M. A.|author=Ibragimov, I. A.|author2=Pełczyński, A.|chapter=Nuclear approximation and approximative dimension|title=Thirty-one invited addresses at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Moscow in 1966|series=American Mathematical Society Translations, Series 2, Vol. 70|pages=137–145|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|year=1968|isbn=978-0-8218-9645-7 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3xQpXJ_hmBMC}}</ref> In 1983, he was a plenary speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Warsaw and gave the talk ''Structural Theory of Banach Spaces and Its Interplay with Analysis and Probability''.
